R0225.title: Webhook Forgery and Event Replay
R0225.definition: Attackers forge or replay webhook events to trigger false payments, shipments, authorizations, or status changes.

references.title: Stripe Webhook Security: Signature Verification and Replay Attack Prevention

R0225.description:
Webhook forgery and event replay occur when receivers fail to validate signatures, timestamps, event IDs, or idempotency state. Attackers can create or repeat events that trigger shipment, recharge, authorization, or state changes.

Asynchronous events connect payments, orders, SaaS integrations, and automation flows. A broken trust boundary can turn forged external messages into internal business actions.
R0225.influence: Forged or replayed callbacks can trigger false payment confirmation, wrong shipment, authorization changes, and accounting inconsistency.

observables: Webhook receivers process events and trigger business actions without signature verification
The same event ID is delivered repeatedly and triggers duplicate fulfillment or status changes
Webhook request timestamps or sources mismatch expectations yet are still accepted
Payment or order status shows inconsistent changes due to forged callbacks
Callback endpoints show duplicate fulfillment caused by idempotency gaps
